institutionName: Western Norway University of Applied Sciences (HVL)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The nature around town was mesmerizing and absolutely beautiful. The exchange programme gave new opportunities for new interesting courses that were relevant for my study and possibly my future work. The facilities in and around the university was everything I wanted. from sport facilities to nature facilities.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy to find information around town. We had an intro zoom meeting before arriving and we were giving a lot of information in that meeting. We also made a WhatsApp group within our class and helped each other a lot.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A nice intro week where we got all the information we needed. And in general the Saman (student organisation) organisation where really helpful.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Super easy. Saman (student organisation) was super easy to navigate in and there where very helpful.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Just the Saman organisation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I registred for the courses via an application form and it was quite easy. the webside of the host institution was easy to navigate in.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: easy webside to follow.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: 100 % succesful. I got exactly what I wanted and with no problems at all.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: follow the instructions and everything will be quite easy.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was at a bachelor degree level. and consisted of two courses with 15 credits each.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was similar to some of my own courses with a combination of theory and practical lessons. And also seminars, group work and individual work. I really enjoyed that.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
My programme was called outdoor education and nordic friluftsliv and consisted of two sub courses:
Friluftsliv, nature and culture and outdoor leadership.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend the two courses that my exchange programme offered. A lot of diverse learning lessons, seminars, practical lessons.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food and drinks was more expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
A lot of student organisations that were super fun.
student sport organisation - studentspretten: opportunities to try new sports and just play sport with other students every week.
Lurkalaget: sport/event/climbing organisation that hosted a lot of nice activities and trips
Sjøspretten: water sport/activity organisation that hosted and planned activities in water.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend all the activities that the host institution offered: they are great at gathering people and is a great opportunity to go on new adventures and socialize.
download the app UT and search for walking routes
Check out DNT cabins and go on trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel and explore the area. Climbing outside. DNT cabins. Walking routes. Snow sport/activities. Surfing in Hodevikk.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was easy because im from Denmark and the culture was not that different and I understood the language and writing.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: attend all local activities. Expand your comfort zone and go to events and trips planned through student organisations.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Enjoy the nature and take care of it
2. Socialize as much as possible and enjoy every moment with the people you meet
3. Do your best with your own capabilities to enjoy it as much as possible

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont be afraid to expand your horizon and try new things that you never tried before.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friends that I got and the adventures and trips I went on.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Going home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
